convention: anthropics/skills/skill-creator evals.json — two kinds. `kind:"trigger"` fixtures carry `should_trigger` for description-optimisation (train/held-out trigger accuracy). `kind:"behavioural"` fixtures carry a `tier` (M/D/R) and `expectations[]` asserting the skill applies / reasons / declines correctly on a Reagent→Hicasso fixture input.
notes: Positives target Reagent-view→Hicasso prompts on an already-re-frame2 app (h/defview, deref-drop, moving off Reagent hiccup). Negatives target the DIFFERENT v1→v2 events/subs/db migration (re-frame-migration), authoring on re-frame2 (re-frame2), greenfield (re-frame2-setup), live runtime (re-frame2-pair), and the first-class 'stay on Reagent' non-goal. Id 13 is DELIBERATELY ABSENT: it was `neg-maintain-ui-views`, a negative routing a `:rf.ui.compile/` question to the `re-frame2-ui` skill, and rf2-0yp7w removed both the substrate (2026-08-16) and that skill — the scenario is unreachable and the destination does not exist. Do NOT renumber to close the gap; ids are referenced by number in this field. Two behavioural fixtures exist specifically to catch OVER-SELLING: the skill must state that the Reagent adapter is first-class and that Hicasso is pre-publication before it starts work. Several exist to catch the failure mode of emitting a spelling a GUIDE PAGE states but the shipped door does not export. The long-standing example, h/fn, was swept to h/event on 2026-08-15 and no page teaches it now, so cite the LIVE one instead: the key-map position restriction, still stated in docs/core/hicasso/03-events-as-data.md and contradicted by impl/intent.cljs's lower-prop. Note also that the draft-guide corpus SHIPPED to docs/core/hicasso/ under rf2-0yp7w, so 'draft guide' no longer names the hazard's location. The SSR/hydration doors are NOT in that set: server/render, ssr/hydrate! and h/hydrate! all shipped under rf2-b6jkj, and eval 23 grades the shipped pipeline rather than a refusal. Eval 23 was re-checked against PR #9147 (rf2-xoal), which added reagent.dom.server to the recognised set and rostered render-to-string as :static-markup: its fixture is that exact call, so the SITE flipped from unrecognised to rostered. No expectation moved and none was added, because 23 grades the SSR pipeline and its expectations never referenced the census or the reporter at all — the fixture's meaning is unchanged, not silently changed. :static-markup's destination is MIG-23, this same leaf, so the roster and the catalogue agree. Expectations are verified against the shipped source under implementation/hicasso/src, not against the design corpus. Eval 25's rf/init! expectation used to justify KEEPING the app's adapter install by asserting that Hicasso ships no adapter of its own; rf2-hvr5h retired that premise (re-frame.hicasso.substrate now declares :kind :rf.adapter/hicasso). The GRADED behaviour never rested on the absence and is unchanged — installation is explicit, there is no default-adapter registry, and a Reagent adapter under a Hicasso tree keeps working exactly as it did — so only the stated reason moved. Do NOT re-grade this fixture as 'switch to the Hicasso adapter': choosing an adapter is not part of this migration. Eval 29 is the COMPLEMENT of that, not a contradiction of it, and the two are distinguished by a precondition rather than by policy: 25 grades a PART-migrated boot, where the install stays; 29 grades the end state where ZERO Reagent views remain and the ADAPTER choice reopens. 29 grades NAMING the option (substrate/adapter) and leaving the decision with the author — an answer that performs the switch, or that recommends it, fails it just as an answer claiming the adapter must stay does. 29 and 30 together carry a correction made under the merged-PR audit of PR #9008, and the pair is the point: 'no Reagent VIEW remains' does NOT establish 'no Reagent remains'. This skill is views-only, so it never read the non-view code, and reagent.core / reagent.ratom use can outlive every converted view. The two coordinates therefore separate — day8/re-frame2-reagent follows from the adapter swap because it ships only re-frame.adapter.reagent, while dropping reagent/reagent is gated on a whole-repository measurement rather than on the view count. 30 is the fixture where that measurement would come back NON-zero: it grades the app that has zero Reagent views and surviving reagent.ratom/run! use, and it exists to catch the build break the inference causes, since reagent/reagent reaches the classpath transitively through day8/re-frame2-reagent and an app relying on that must ADD a direct entry when the adapter coordinate goes. Do NOT re-collapse 29 and 30 into a single 'can I drop Reagent' fixture: the whole content of the correction is that the answer differs between them. 31 carries a second correction, from the merged-PR audit of PR #9036, and it is about WHICH NUMBER the measurement reads: the reporter's declared estimand (migration/reagent-to-hicasso/codemod/src/re_frame/migration/hicasso/census.clj) is 'Rostered view-substrate API call sites, addressed at the CALL', so a call-site count cannot prove dependency ABSENCE — a Reagent Var referenced as a value, (def factory r/atom), scans as zero entries with :reagent? true and :unresolved? false while the build still needs the coordinate. The licence is therefore the reporter's files-that-name-Reagent half plus a textual/dependency-config sweep, and 31 is the fixture that fails an answer resting on zero call sites. Do NOT re-grade 31 as a reporter bug: the reporter reports what it claims to, and already exposes files-with-reagent. Eval 28 exists because rf2-6c12m.15 removed h/use-subs and internalised the navigate head (re-frame.hicasso.impl.intent/navigate, minted by h/route-link): it fails an answer that emits either retired form and passes one that stays on the live doors — h/sub at each read site, h/route-link or an ordinary routing event for navigation.

evals.name: m-does-not-oversell-the-need
evals.prompt: We're moving our re-frame v1 app to re-frame2. Should I rewrite all my Reagent views into Hicasso as part of that?
expectations: Answers NO to the premise: the v1→v2 move leaves views on the first-class Reagent adapter (day8/re-frame2-reagent, the default browser substrate) and is COMPLETE at that point — no view rewrite is required to land on re-frame2.

States that rewriting into Hicasso is a separate, OPTIONAL second step chosen for what Hicasso offers, and that it is a rewrite (props become one map, handlers become data, state leaves the component), not a respelling.

States that Hicasso is PRE-PUBLICATION with no released Maven coordinate, so a project can adopt it only from source: day8/re-frame2-hicasso is not published and there is no date at which it will be, and the installation page resolves it by :local/root from a checkout. An answer saying there is NO coordinate to quote passes; do NOT require it to say a printed coordinate fails to resolve, because the page prints none.

Gives the trade in both directions rather than advocating: what the rewrite buys (handlers as data, value-returning ambient sub, one boundary model, declared foreign-React crossings, IME-gated key maps) against what it costs (no view-local state tier, no component-did-update, provisional spellings).
Routes the v1→v2 work to re-frame-migration and does NOT start converting views.
Does not imply the author 'should' move or describe staying on Reagent as half-migrated.

evals.name: m-transform-defview-sub-lift
evals.prompt:
Convert this to Hicasso — I'm on re-frame2 and I've decided I want it:
(defn price [amt cur] [:button {:on-click #(dispatch [:buy amt])} @(subscribe [:total])])
(defn app [] [:div [price 1 2]])
expectations: Rewrites the header to (h/defview price [{:keys [amt cur]}] ...) — positional params become one destructured props map (MIG-01).
Declares the props parameter on the zero-prop view as [_] and rewrites the call site atomically to [price {:amt 1 :cur 2}] in the same change (MIG-01).
Drops the deref: @(subscribe [:total]) becomes (h/sub [:total]) (MIG-02).
Lifts the handler: {:on-click #(dispatch [:buy amt])} becomes {:on-click [:buy amt]} (MIG-04).
Adds the require [re-frame.hicasso :as h] (MIG-24) and cites the MIG ids for each change.
Notes the `h` alias is load-bearing because ::h/value / ::h/checked / ::h/prevent auto-resolve through it.
Does NOT treat the event vector [:buy amt] or the query vector [:total] as hiccup to respell or forward.
Does NOT invent a {:compiled true} option, a v/ alias, or any Freehand spelling.

evals.name: m-leftover-closure-is-a-click-time-failure
evals.prompt:
I converted this view to Hicasso and it compiles and renders, but clicking Save throws :rf.error/no-frame-context. Why?
(h/defview save-btn [_] [:button {:on-click #(rf/dispatch [:save])} "Save"])
expectations: Identifies the leftover Reagent closure as the cause: an unmarked plain function at an on-* prop is passed through to React BY IDENTITY, deliberately, so React.memo and handler-identity bail-outs keep working — nothing refuses it at lowering or at render.
Explains the timing: when the browser invokes it later the render extent has unwound, ambient dispatch has no frame to resolve against, and the failure lands at click time.
Notes the id is core's :rf.error/no-frame-context, not a :rf.error/hicasso-* one, so grepping for Hicasso diagnostics will not find it.
Fixes it to the event vector {:on-click [:save]} (MIG-04), or to h/event where the callback genuinely needs the event (MIG-18).
Advises grepping the converted bodies for surviving closures rather than finding them by clicking, and connects that to the whole-view-coherence rule.

Distinguishes this CLICK-time id from the RENDER-time one: a leftover ambient rf/subscribe or rf/dispatch still inside the render extent — the body OR a helper it inlines — refuses at first render with :rf.error/ambient-frame-refused, a DIFFERENT id, because a refused ambient read and a genuinely frameless one are different mistakes. Does not report the render-time refusal as :rf.error/no-frame-context, and does not claim this click-time failure would have been caught at render.

evals.name: m-key-metadata-is-never-read
evals.prompt:
Migrate to Hicasso:
(defn item [t] [:li t])
(defn lst [ts] [:ul (doall (for [t ts] ^{:key (:id t)} [item t]))])
expectations: Converts item and lst to h/defview and moves ^{:key (:id t)} into the props map as [item {:key (:id t) :t t}] (MIG-07).

States that Hicasso performs NO metadata read anywhere in the codec, so a surviving ^{:key ...} is an ABSENT key rather than a spelling variant — React then reconciles by position, which is silent state corruption in a reorderable or filterable list.

Notes that a missing key gets React's own warning (Hicasso adds no missing-key diagnostic of its own), while a map or other entity value at :key on a boundary-headed member gets :rf.warning/hicasso-entity-key.
Strips the doall (MIG-12).
Does NOT treat the bare symbol child in [:li t] as a props map — `t` is content, never forwarded (the bare-symbol trap).
Notes that :key is read as the exact literal keyword, so "key" and :x/key are ordinary attributes rather than the key.

evals.name: d-decide-form2-local-state
evals.prompt:
Migrate this Reagent view to Hicasso:
(defn dropdown [] (r/with-let [open? (r/atom false)] [:div {:on-click #(reset! open? true)} (when @open? [:ul])]))
expectations: Recognises Form-2 / with-let view-held state (MIG-16) and does NOT silently rewrite the view.

States that Hicasso has NO view-local state tier at all — no local, no use-state, no cell — and that an atom in a defview body is re-allocated every render because the body is an anonymous fn React re-invokes; does not emit one.

Reasons about the real decision: product state or a UI flag → app-db, with h/reg-state as the sugar; a draft-and-commit control → re-frame.hicasso.forms/buffered-field; state genuinely the DOM's → a callback ref or a React island.
For a simple open/closed flag, lands on app-db via h/reg-state rather than treating 'it's only ephemeral' as a reason to keep it in the view.

If it shows h/reg-state, gets the shape right: a namespace-qualified concern, an optional {:default ...}, a parametric sub read as (h/sub [concern ikey]) and a setter event dispatched as [concern ikey v], stored under [:ui ::concern ikey].
Holds the WHOLE view until the decision is made (cardinal rule 2).
Does not reach into the dataflow layer itself; it names what the author must write.

evals.name: d-mig17-lifecycle-ref-and-rehome
evals.prompt:
Migrate this Reagent Form-3 view to Hicasso:
(ns app.editor (:require [reagent.core :as r] [reagent.dom :as rdom]))
(defn editor []
  (r/create-class
   {:component-did-mount    (fn [this] (.focus (rdom/dom-node this)))
    :component-will-unmount (fn [_] (rf/dispatch [:resource/release]))
    :should-component-update (fn [_ _ _] true)
    :reagent-render         (fn [] [editor-form])}))
expectations: Recognises MIG-17 Form-3 lifecycle and decomposes each body into host/DOM work vs domain work — a judgment call held WHOLE, not an automatic rewrite.
Deletes :should-component-update as dead under memoised boundaries, and extracts :reagent-render as the view body.
Routes the focus-on-mount DOM work to a CALLBACK REF — a function at :ref, React's own contract, called with the node at commit, whose RETURN VALUE is the detach cleanup.
Insists the ref fn be a stable top-level def, because a fresh inline (fn [n] ...) has a new identity every render and React detaches and reattaches on every commit.

Notes a VECTOR at :ref is not a ref — it crosses to React as data and never fires, so the callback function is the only spelling — and that :ref on a defview HEAD is not a ref at all — the boundary path lifts only :key.

Recognises there is no dispatch-at-unmount: re-homes the [:resource/release] domain work OUT of the view to whatever causally ends the resource, and enumerates EVERY exit path — an enumeration covering save/delete but missing navigate-away is the classic leak.

Does NOT emit `effect`, a Freehand behavior, v/defbehavior, or a React hook inside the defview body; if hook-shaped lifecycle is genuinely needed it names the island route — a UIx defui or a raw React function component mounted through h/defhost, using n/use-sub / n/use-frame when it needs Hicasso state — where React's rules of hooks apply to source the author controls.

evals.name: d-foreign-react-defhost-and-contracts
evals.prompt:
Migrate this view to Hicasso:
(ns app.picker (:require ["react-datepicker" :default DatePicker]))
(defn booking [] [:div [:> DatePicker {:selected @(subscribe [:date]) :onChange #(dispatch [:date/set %])}]])
expectations: Does NOT decline: [:> Component ...] is legal in Hicasso and still works, so a foreign React component never forces the view onto Reagent.
Frames the decision as which door: keep [:>] for a one-off crossing, declare a repeated crossing once with h/defhost so the var becomes a legal hiccup head.

States that the callback contract is INFERRED from the prop's spelling exactly as on a native tag (on* is an event position, anything else a render position, a plain function crosses untouched), so the usual defhost needs no :callbacks at all — and warns that a vendor's on*-named render prop (Fluent onRender*, Ant onRow) would infer :event, whose wrapper returns nil and blanks the UI, so that prop gets a {:callbacks {... :render}} override. Says to check every on* prop's return value against the library's documentation. Does not offer a :handler contract.

Gets the argument law right: react-datepicker calls onChange(date, event) — VALUE-first — so an intent vector with ::h/value would raise :rf.error/hicasso-intent-needs-the-event, and the spelling is h/event, which receives every argument the invoker passed in order.
Turns the @(subscribe [:date]) deref into a render-time (h/sub [:date]) read feeding :selected.

Notes an intent vector at an on* prop of a former Reagent crossing now DISPATCHES, and that under Reagent that vector crossed as an inert JS array so it never worked — the migration turns a dead handler live, so decide whether it was ever meant to run.

Recommends running the migration reporter over the codebase for the rest of the [:>] prop-dialect differences, and reads its defhost sketches as a list of positions to check rather than a declaration to paste.

evals.name: d-mig28-computed-props-are-a-plain-merge-owned-last
evals.prompt:
Migrate this reusable control to Hicasso:
(defn text-field [attrs draft on-change]
  [:input (merge attrs {:type "text" :value (:title draft) :on-change on-change})])
expectations: Recognises MIG-28 and keeps a plain merge with the field's owned keys LAST: [:input (merge (dissoc attrs :key) {:type "text" :value ... :on-change ...})] — there is no reserved merge key and no spread form in Hicasso.
States that the owned literals win by presence because they are merged last, so a caller cannot replace :value or :on-change by forwarding the same key.

Notes that :key and ::h/revision belong to the wrapper's element and are dissoc'd from the forwarded map rather than passed through, and that the case where a caller override SHOULD win is spelled by not writing the owned literal.
Notes that forwarded maps use the same kebab-keyword spelling as the literals — an alternate spelling of one React slot is a different map key, and which lands is then map order rather than law.
Does NOT emit a reserved :& key, and does NOT invent spread / spread-safe verbs — those are a different substrate's.

evals.name: d-ssr-hydrate-pipeline-ships
evals.prompt:
Migrate this to Hicasso:
(ns app.render (:require [reagent.dom.server :as s]))
(defn render-page [] (s/render-to-string [app]))
;; the client then hydrates that markup
expectations: Routes this to MIG-23 as a D-tier DECISION and does NOT decline it for want of a door: re-frame.hicasso.server is a shipped optional module whose product door is render, and both client doors exist — re-frame.ssr/hydrate! for state and h/hydrate! for the DOM.

States the cold two-process boot condition: the Node renderer and the browser are SEPARATE, freshly booted processes, nothing installs an adapter for either (there is no default-adapter registry), and server/render mints a frame per request — so the server namespace installs (rf/init! ssr/adapter) ONCE at process startup before the first server/render, never per request, or frame construction raises :rf.error/no-adapter-installed before any HTML is produced; a cold client entry that omits its own install fails at its first rf/make-frame the same way.

Keeps the migrating app's EXISTING Reagent adapter install on the client — (rf/init! reagent-adapter/adapter) before rf/make-frame — as a boot precondition distinguished from the three hydration operations, and does NOT silently switch a part-migrated app to another adapter: adapter selection is not part of this migration.

Teaches the client boot as THREE ordered calls after that precondition — rf/make-frame creates the frame, ssr/hydrate! replaces its state from the __rf_payload script, then h/hydrate! adopts the server DOM — and gives the ordering's reason: h/hydrate! does NOT ensure the frame the way h/mount! does, so without make-frame the :rf/hydrate dispatch is a silent no-op and the page renders empty.
Names server/render's two REQUIRED opts, :hiccup and :payload, and that :payload is the fail-closed allowlist of the top-level app-db keys the page reads.
Names the :identifier-prefix contract: the same string goes to server/render and to that root's h/hydrate!, or every useId-generated id in the root resolves differently from the bytes it is adopting.

Puts the real decision where it belongs — INFRASTRUCTURE, not spelling: React renders the server output and there is no parallel JVM string emitter, so the renderer runs on Node, and an app whose SSR is a JVM handler today is deciding whether to stand up a Node rendering service. A per-root hold on Reagent remains honest if the answer is no.
Does NOT state that the server namespace, server/render, ssr/hydrate! or h/hydrate! is missing.

evals.name: r-decline-prev-props-update-protocol
evals.prompt:
Convert this view to Hicasso:
(r/create-class
 {:get-snapshot-before-update (fn [this _] (.-scrollHeight (rdom/dom-node this)))
  :component-did-update       (fn [this _ snapshot] (restore-scroll! (rdom/dom-node this) snapshot))
  :reagent-render             (fn [] [:div.feed])})
expectations: Declines (MIG-36): Hicasso has no component-did-update mechanism and no previous-props channel — re-render IS the update, and nothing hands a body the old values.
Notes get-snapshot-before-update in particular has no counterpart, because there is no pre-mutation moment to hook.

Names the two honest routes before holding: a React island (a UIx defui or a raw React function component mounted through h/defhost, with n/use-sub / n/use-frame for Hicasso state) with react/useEffect and a dependency array where the work is genuinely the DOM's, or app-db where the 'previous value' is really domain history the changing event already knows.
Holds the WHOLE view on Reagent and states that as a supported configuration.
Does NOT reach for a callback ref as a substitute — a ref fires on commit and on identity change, which is a different phase and frequency.

evals.name: m-root-mount-ensures-frame
evals.prompt:
Migrate the boot for this app to Hicasso:
(ns app.core (:require [reagent.dom :as rdom] [re-frame.core :as rf] [re-frame.adapter.reagent :as ra]))
(defn init! []
  (rf/init! ra/adapter)
  (rf/dispatch-sync [:app/init])
  (rdom/render [app] (js/document.getElementById "root")))
expectations: Collapses the boot into ONE mount: (h/mount! el {:frame ::frame :initial-events [[:app/init]]} [app {}]) — the dispatch-sync seed becomes :initial-events, because mounting ENSURES the frame and seeds it before the first paint.
States h/mount! takes a CONFIG MAP — (container config hiccup) — carrying :frame, optional :initial-events, and optional :identifier-prefix.

KEEPS (rf/init! ra/adapter): frame construction raises :rf.error/no-adapter-installed until a reactive adapter is installed, nothing installs one for you (there is no default-adapter registry), and a Reagent adapter under a Hicasso tree keeps working exactly as it did. Does not delete it as Reagent scaffolding.

Adds the defonce root atom and a ^:dev/after-load hook calling (h/render! @!root [app {}]), and explains that calling h/mount! again would createRoot a second time and replace the tree, discarding every node and scrap of component state.

An explicit (rf/make-frame {:id ::frame :initial-events [[:app/init]]}) BEFORE the mount is also acceptable — the mount then joins the live frame without re-seeding — but it must not be presented as REQUIRED, and the mount must not be shown as positional.

evals.name: m-keystroke-handler-becomes-key-map
evals.prompt:
Migrate this Reagent handler to Hicasso:
[:input {:on-key-down (fn [e] (case (.-key e)
                                "Enter"  (dispatch [:commit id])
                                "Escape" (dispatch [:cancel id])
                                nil))}]
expectations: Rewrites to the key map {:on-key-down {"Enter" [:commit id] "Escape" [:cancel id]}} (MIG-33), with keys as the browser's own .key strings.

States the rewrite also FIXES a bug: the whole map is composition-gated, so a keystroke arriving mid-IME-composition commits nothing — which is the half the hand-written .key test does not have, and it is wrong for every user who composes.
Notes a branch value that is neither a vector nor a function is SILENTLY dropped.
Notes a key map at :on-submit auto-prevents on every branch, because the position is passed down.
Does NOT claim key maps are restricted to :on-key-down / :on-key-up — the guide still says so (docs/core/hicasso/03-events-as-data.md) and the shipped lowering accepts a map at any event position.

evals.name: m-dangerous-html-converts-but-goes-live
evals.prompt:
Migrate this to Hicasso:
(defn article-body [html] [:div.body {:dangerouslySetInnerHTML {:__html html}}])
expectations: Converts the view with NO change to the prop: Hicasso has no trusted-markup verb and needs none — :dangerouslySetInnerHTML is an ordinary prop that passes straight through to React.

FLAGS it rather than skipping it (MIG-34): Reagent DELETED this prop unless it was wrapped, and Hicasso passes it through, so a site that was inert becomes live — markup that may never have been injected starts being injected.
Puts the question to the author that matters: is this string still trusted, and is whatever cleared it still clearing it — because for these sites that path may never have been exercised.
Notes only the camel spelling reaches React: :dangerously-set-inner-html emits dangerouslySetInnerHtml and :inner-html emits innerHtml, both of which React ignores.
Notes the codemod reports every such site as :dangerous-html, a runtime blocker, for this reason.
Does NOT emit v/html or any other trusted-markup verb — that belongs to a different substrate and Hicasso exports nothing of the kind.

evals.name: m-live-doors-sub-per-site-no-navigate-head
evals.prompt:
Convert this to Hicasso — I'm on re-frame2 and I've decided I want it:
(defn nav-panel []
  (let [total @(subscribe [:total]) items @(subscribe [:items])]
    [:nav
     [:a {:href "/all" :on-click (fn [e] (.preventDefault e) (dispatch [:route/set :all]))} "All (" total ")"]
     (when (seq items) [:span (count items)])]))
expectations: Every subscription read becomes an (h/sub ...) call at its own read site (MIG-02) — the let of derefs dissolves into ordinary reads, legal inside the when because h/sub is the ambient collector.

Does NOT emit h/use-subs or any other grouped-read form: the shipped door (implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso.cljc) exports sub and nothing else for reads — the grouped read was removed by rf2-6c12m.15.
Handles the anchor on a live door: h/route-link where a routing module owns the URL, or a plain anchor whose click is [::h/prevent [:route/set :all]] (MIG-06) — an ordinary routing event.

Does NOT emit ::h/navigate anywhere: the navigate head is implementation-owned (re-frame.hicasso.impl.intent/navigate), h/route-link mints it, and an authored ::h/navigate resolves to a different keyword the intent lowering does not recognise as its navigation head.
Lifts nothing else half-way: the .preventDefault closure becomes the ::h/prevent head wrapping the intent vector, not a surviving plain fn.

evals.name: m-completed-migration-adapter-choice-reopens
evals.prompt: That was the last one — every view in the app is Hicasso now, no Reagent views left anywhere. Can I drop Reagent from deps.edn?
expectations: Does NOT say the Reagent adapter must stay: MIG-15's 'the install stays' governs a migration IN PROGRESS, and the app has finished, so the adapter question is now genuinely open.

Names re-frame.hicasso.substrate/adapter (:kind :rf.adapter/hicasso) as the replacement, with the require [re-frame.hicasso.substrate :as substrate] and the one boot line (rf/init! substrate/adapter) in place of the Reagent adapter install.

SPLITS the question into two decisions instead of retiring both coordinates on the view count. day8/re-frame2-reagent follows from the adapter swap, because it ships exactly one namespace (re-frame.adapter.reagent); dropping reagent/reagent does NOT follow, because this skill is views-only (cardinal rule 5) and never read the non-view code. An answer that retires both as a single consequence of 'no views left' FAILS.

Gates the reagent/reagent half on a MEASUREMENT rather than an inference, and on the RIGHT half of the reporter's line: zero FILES naming a recognised Reagent namespace (after removing proven-orphan requires) and no UNRESOLVED clause, paired with a plain textual sweep of the whole repository — sources and dependency/build config alike — for non-call references. An answer resting the decision on 'zero view-substrate API CALL SITES' FAILS: the reporter's declared estimand is rostered view-substrate API call sites addressed at the CALL, so a Reagent Var used as a value — (def factory r/atom) — censuses as zero calls with no UNRESOLVED while the build still needs the coordinate. Naming the instrument AND reading its files half is what passes; asserting the coordinate is dead without a measurement does not.

Names the classpath coupling, which runs the surprising way: day8/re-frame2-reagent is what puts reagent/reagent on the classpath (it declares the stock dep; core declares none), so an app that never listed Reagent itself and still calls r/atom somewhere BREAKS when the adapter coordinate goes, and the repair is to ADD a direct reagent/reagent entry rather than remove one.

Leaves both calls as the AUTHOR'S decision rather than performing or recommending them: keeping the Reagent adapter is a complete, supported configuration, and an app that may grow a Reagent or UIx subtree later has a standing reason to keep it (cardinal rule 5).
States the precondition honestly: none of this arises while even one held R-tier or D-tier Reagent view remains — then the adapter and both coordinates stay.

evals.name: m-zero-views-but-reagent-survives-outside-them
evals.prompt: Every view is Hicasso now — nothing renders through Reagent anywhere. We do still call reagent.ratom/run! in app.watchers and r/atom in a couple of non-view helpers. Can I drop day8/re-frame2-reagent and reagent from deps.edn?
expectations: Answers the two halves DIFFERENTLY rather than as one yes/no. An answer that says 'yes, drop both' fails, and so does one that says 'no, keep both' — the adapter half and the reagent/reagent half have different answers here.

day8/re-frame2-reagent CAN go: no view renders through Reagent, so the substrate install can move to (rf/init! substrate/adapter) from [re-frame.hicasso.substrate :as substrate], which ships inside day8/re-frame2-hicasso and costs no new coordinate.

reagent/reagent MUST STAY: reagent.ratom/run! and r/atom are live Reagent API call sites, and this skill is views-only (cardinal rule 5) — it converted the views and never had a mandate over app.watchers or the helpers. Zero Reagent views is not zero Reagent.

Catches the build break, which is the whole point of the fixture: reagent/reagent is on the classpath TRANSITIVELY via day8/re-frame2-reagent, so dropping that artefact while those call sites live breaks the build unless the app declares reagent/reagent directly. The instruction is to ADD that entry as part of the swap, not to remove one.

Does NOT volunteer to migrate app.watchers or the helpers off Reagent. Naming them as what keeps the dependency is correct; converting non-view Reagent code is outside this skill, and an answer that rewrites reagent.ratom/run! into a Hicasso or re-frame form fails cardinal rule 5.

evals.name: m-zero-call-sites-but-reagent-var-used-as-a-value
evals.prompt: Every view is Hicasso now. I ran the reporter over the whole repo and it says "0 view-substrate API call site(s) across 1 file(s) that name Reagent and 0 that name a re-frame2 adapter — 0 mechanical, 0 human-decision, 0 runtime-blocker — ZERO ENTRIES: bounded by the ROSTER, not by the corpus; read :census :summary :caveat" with no UNRESOLVED line — the one file is app.core, which has (:require [reagent.core :as r]) and (def factory r/atom); we pass factory around and call it later. Safe to drop day8/re-frame2-reagent and reagent from deps.edn?
expectations: reagent/reagent MUST STAY, and the zero call-site count is NOT a licence to drop it. An answer reading '0 call sites, no UNRESOLVED' as proof the coordinate is dead FAILS — this fixture exists for exactly that mistake.
Reads the FILES half of the reporter's own line: 1 file still names a recognised Reagent namespace, so the coordinate stays whatever the call count says. Zero calls is not zero references.

Names WHY the census reads zero: the reporter's declared estimand is rostered view-substrate API call sites addressed at the CALL, and r/atom here is passed as a VALUE, never in call-head position. The same blind spot covers Vars handed around, type/protocol references, and build/preload configuration outside scanned CLJS call heads.

Does NOT blame the reporter or ask for it to be changed: it reports what it claims to report, and already exposes the distinction as files-that-name-Reagent. The defect under test is reading a call-site estimate as a dependency proof.

day8/re-frame2-reagent can still go on the adapter argument alone (no view renders through Reagent, so (rf/init! substrate/adapter) replaces the install) — but ONLY with a direct reagent/reagent entry ADDED, since that artefact is what puts Reagent on the classpath transitively and factory still resolves reagent.core/atom.
Leaves the call to the author (cardinal rule 5) and does not offer to rewrite app.core off Reagent: this skill is views-only and app.core's helper is not a view.
